// A corpus for the parity check: every lexer hazard in the scanner, plus enough ordinary
// nesting that the identity, colour and trait rolls all get exercised.
using System;

namespace Sample
{
    public class Orders
    {
        // A line comment with braces in it: { } ( ) [ ]
        /* A block comment
           spanning lines with { } inside */

        private readonly string _verbatim = @"a verbatim { string "" with doubled quotes }";
        private readonly string _interp = $"an interpolated {hole} that is opaque";
        private readonly string _both = $@"both prefixes {here} too";
        private readonly string _raw = """
            a raw string { with braces } across lines
            """;

        public async Task<Order> GetOrderAsync(int id)
        {
            if (id < 0)
            {
                throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(id));
            }

            var items = new List<Item>
            {
                new Item { Sku = "a[0]", Qty = 1 },
                new Item { Sku = "b{1}", Qty = 2 },
            };

            char open = '{';
            char close = '}';
            char escaped = '\'';

            return await _store.FindAsync(id, items, open, close, escaped);
        }

        public void Deeply()
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
            {
                while (true)
                {
                    if (i % 2 == 0)
                    {
                        switch (i)
                        {
                            case 0:
                            {
                                Console.WriteLine("zero");
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        public void Same() { }
        public void Same2() { }
    }
}

// JavaScript, so the template-literal and single-quote paths are hit too.
const build = (rows) => {
    const label = `row ${rows.length} of {many}`;
    const single = 'a string with { and } in it';
    const lifetime = "not a lifetime, but this is: &'a str";
    return rows.map((r, i) => ({ id: r.id, label, index: i }));
};

function unbalanced() {
    const a = [1, 2, 3];
    if (a.length) {
        return a.map((x) => x * 2);
    // deliberately unclosed, so the unmatched path has something to question
